Per-Sequence Indices

Source: R/sequence_metrics.R
sequence_metrics.Rd

sequence_metrics() computes descriptive indices for every sequence and returns one row per sequence: length and validity, composition and diversity, spells, transitions, the fate of the initial state, the dominant and emergent states, cyclic recurrence and a composite complexity index, plus the integrative potential of a set of favourable states when favorable is given. It reads any input extract_sequences() reads: a wide table of positions, an event log, the output of prepare(), a sequence network or group of networks, or a tna model. The indices are those of codyna::sequence_indices(), with three corrections listed under Details.

The indices describe each sequence as it was observed, and several of them (spells, transitions, recurrence) rest on few positions in a short sequence; read them beside valid_n. Because there is one row per sequence, the result can be summarised, plotted or used as predictors; sequence_patterns() and pattern_outcome() look at which subsequences recur and how they relate to an outcome.

Usage

sequence_metrics(
  x,
  favorable = NULL,
  omega = 1,
  meta = FALSE,
  cols = NULL,
  actor = NULL,
  action = NULL,
  time = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

The sequence data, in any form extract_sequences() accepts.

favorable

The favourable states; giving them adds integrative_potential. States that do not occur in the data are ignored, and an error of class nestimate_bad_input is raised when none of them occur. Default NULL.

omega

The exponent of the position weights in integrative_potential; a positive value gives later positions more weight, 0 weights every position equally and a negative value gives earlier positions more weight; any single finite number is accepted. Ignored without favorable. Default 1.

meta

Whether to put each sequence's covariates (actor, session, group, metadata) before the indices. Default FALSE.

cols

The state columns of a wide data frame, as in extract_sequences(). Default NULL.

actor, action, time

The actor, action and timestamp columns of a long event log, as in extract_sequences(): setting action declares x an event log. Default NULL.

...

Further arguments passed to prepare() for a long event log, such as time_threshold or order.

Value

A data frame with one row per sequence, in the order of extract_sequences(), and the columns described in Details (integrative_potential only with favorable). With meta = TRUE, the input's covariate columns, if it has any, come first.

Details

Positions after a sequence's last observed state are not part of it; p below is the position of the last observed state.

valid_n, valid_proportion

The number of observed states, and their share of the first p positions.

unique_states

The number of distinct states.

mean_spell_duration, max_spell_duration

The mean and the longest run of one state.

longitudinal_entropy

The Shannon entropy of the state proportions, divided by the log of the number of states in the data (0 to 1; 0 when the data hold one state).

simpson_diversity

One minus the sum of squared proportions.

self_loop_tendency, transition_rate

The share of transitions (pairs of adjacent observed states) that repeat the state, and the share that change it; the two sum to 1.

transition_complexity

The number of distinct state-changing transitions, as a share of the \(a(a - 1)\) possible ones, where \(a\) is the number of states in the data; NA when the data hold one state.

initial_state_persistence

The length of the opening spell as a share of p.

initial_state_proportion

The share of the observed states that are the first state.

initial_state_influence_decay

The share of the first third spent in the first state minus the share of the last third.

cyclic_feedback_strength

The largest share, over lags of 2 or more, of positions whose state recurs that many steps later.

first_state, last_state, dominant_state, dominant_proportion, dominant_max_spell

The opening and closing states; the most frequent state (ties go to the state that sorts first), its share and its longest spell.

emergent_state, emergent_state_persistence, emergent_state_proportion

A state that settles in later, its spell and its share; NA when there is none. The candidates are a spell of at least 3 that outlasts the dominant spell, the dominant state when it is not the first and has a spell of at least 3, and a return to the first state in a spell of at least 3 and more than half the opening one; the longest of them is taken.

integrative_potential

With favorable: the position-weighted share of favourable states over the observed positions, with weights position^omega (Brzinsky-Fay 2018).

complexity_index

0.4 * longitudinal_entropy + 0.4 * transition_rate + 0.2 * min(CV of spell durations, 1); 0 for a sequence of one spell (one state, no change). This is codyna's composite, not the complexity index of Gabadinho et al. (2011) that TraMineR::seqici() computes.

Missing values: a missing position is not an observation. The first state is the first observed one, a missing position inside a sequence ends a spell, and a pair of states across it is not a transition. Indices that are undefined for a sequence (for example a rate with no transition) are NA; a sequence with no observed state has valid_n and unique_states 0 and every other index NA. On sequences without internal gaps the indices shared with TraMineR (seqindic(), seqistatd(), seqdur(), seqintegr()) agree exactly; at an internal gap TraMineR joins the states on either side into one sequence, so spells and transitions differ there.

Corrections relative to codyna::sequence_indices() 1.0.0, which otherwise agrees value for value: dominant_max_spell is computed per sequence (codyna reports the last sequence's value for every row); longitudinal_entropy is normalised by the log of the number of states (codyna counts NA as one when the data have missing values); and complexity_index uses the normalised entropy once (codyna divides it by the log of the number of states a second time) and is 0, not NA, for a single spell. Leading and internal missing values follow the rule above, where codyna reads position 1 as the first state and counts missing positions as unfavourable and as possible transitions.

References

Saqr, M., Tikka, S., & López-Pernas, S. (2026). codyna: Complex Dynamic Systems. R package version 1.0.0.

Brzinsky-Fay, C. (2018). Unused resources: Sequence and trajectory indicators. International Symposium on Sequence Analysis and Related Methods, Monte Verità.

Gabadinho, A., Ritschard, G., Müller, N. S., & Studer, M. (2011). Analyzing and visualizing state sequences in R with TraMineR. Journal of Statistical Software, 40(4), 1-37. doi:10.18637/jss.v040.i04
